newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia grain prices mixed on stocks, ringgit.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia grain prices mixed on stocks, ringgit.

text.p: Malaysian grain prices were mixed this week, with the trend influenced by a weak ringgit and poor consumer demand, traders said on Tuesday.
Chinese corn and American wheat prices were quoted slightly lower and Argentine maize rose a trifle while soymeal rates were steady, said traders.
"The adjustments are purely due to the currency fluctuation," said a trader.
"There are no other factors as demand is pretty stable," he added.

The ringgit has fallen sharply against the U.S. dollar in the last fortnight, forcing price adjustments in all commodities in Malaysia. On Tuesday, the currency closed at 2.6220 in Kuala Lumpur after opening at 2.6160.
Traders said Chinese origin bulk corn in Malaysia's central region was quoted at 360-365 ringgit ($137-$139) a tonne C and F this week, compared to 360-375 a week ago.
Bulk Argentine maize, ex-factories/godowns in the central region, was also trading at 365-370 ringgit compared to 360-370 last week.
Fresh arrivals of about 80,000 tonnes of corn this week kept the maize market bearish, said traders.
"A" grade wheat in Malaysia was lower at 650 ringgit a bag from 690 a week ago. "B" grade, however, rose to 430 ringgit from 350.
Soymeal prices were stable at 865 ringgit for imported material.
